bull.b: The large multi-year backlog provides meaningful visibility into future module shipments and revenue, reducing reliance on immediate spot-market demand. Deliveries extending through 2030 also support capacity planning and reinforce First Solar’s position with utility-scale customers.

Very strong gross and EBITDA margins demonstrate substantial current earnings power, particularly as the U.S.-produced module mix expands. If supported by domestic production scale and contract pricing, this profitability can fund technology investment and capacity growth.

Extremely low leverage and strong returns on equity give First Solar considerable financial flexibility without relying heavily on debt. This balance-sheet resilience can support manufacturing expansion, research spending, and shareholder returns while reducing solvency risk.

bear.b: Lowered volume, revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance indicates that near-term demand and delivery timing are weaker than previously expected. A slower growth cadence could reduce operating leverage and make future earnings more dependent on execution and customer commitments.

Recent cash generation is materially weaker than reported earnings, creating a quality risk even though profitability remains high. Persistently low conversion could constrain internally funded expansion and make results more sensitive to working-capital timing and investment needs.

Regulatory uncertainty can delay customer procurement decisions, complicate pricing, and alter the relative economics of domestic production. Because First Solar’s demand and contract terms are closely tied to trade policy, prolonged uncertainty may moderate bookings and utilization.
